events.title: Birth of Neurologist Hermann Oppenheim
events.summary: German neurologist Hermann Oppenheim was born; he later described the Oppenheim reflex and Oppenheim disease, advancing clinical neurological examination.
events.sourceTitle: January 1 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pediatrician Guido Fanconi
events.summary: Swiss pediatrician Guido Fanconi was born; he went on to describe Fanconi anemia in 1927 and made foundational contributions to pediatric hematology and nephrology.
events.sourceTitle: January 1 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Sir Charles Bell Demonstrates Facial Nerve Palsy
events.summary: Scottish anatomist and surgeon Sir Charles Bell publicly demonstrated his first classic case of facial nerve palsy, later known as Bell's palsy, before students at Middlesex Hospital.
events.sourceTitle: January 2 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Christiaan Barnard Performs Second Human Heart Transplant
events.summary: South African surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed his second human heart transplant at Groote Schuur Hospital on patient Philip Blaiberg, who survived for 593 days and helped prove long-term viability.
events.sourceTitle: Norman E. Shumway and the Early Heart Transplants - PMC

events.title: Foundation of the March of Dimes
events.summary: U.S. President Franklin D. Roosevelt established the National Foundation for Infantile Paralysis, later known as the March of Dimes, to fund polio research and patient care.
events.sourceTitle: January 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Bionic Hand with Sense of Touch Unveiled Outside a Lab
events.summary: Researchers in Rome unveiled the first bionic hand equipped with sensory feedback capable of being used outside a laboratory setting, marking a milestone in neuroprosthetics.
events.sourceTitle: January 3 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Death of American Neurologist Silas Weir Mitchell
events.summary: American physician Silas Weir Mitchell, who first described causalgia (complex regional pain syndrome), phantom limb pain, and erythromelalgia, died on this day.
events.sourceTitle: January 4 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: World Braille Day Established
events.summary: The United Nations observed World Braille Day to celebrate the birth of Louis Braille and promote accessible communication and health literacy for people with visual impairments.
events.sourceTitle: January 4 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Public Announcement of Wilhelm Röntgen's Discovery of X-Rays
events.summary: The Vienna newspaper Die Presse published a front-page report announcing Wilhelm Röntgen's discovery of X-rays, sparking immediate global excitement for medical imaging.
events.sourceTitle: January 5 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Clinical Examination of Kawasaki Disease
events.summary: Japanese pediatrician Tomisaku Kawasaki examined a four-year-old boy presenting with a distinctive febrile vasculitis syndrome, marking the first clinical recognition of Kawasaki disease.
events.sourceTitle: January 5 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Adult Human Heart Transplant in the United States
events.summary: Cardiothoracic surgeon Norman E. Shumway performed the first adult human-to-human heart transplant in the United States at Stanford University School of Medicine.
events.sourceTitle: Norman E. Shumway and the Early Heart Transplants - PMC

events.title: Birth of English Surgeon Sir Percivall Pott
events.summary: English surgeon Sir Percivall Pott was born; he later described Pott fracture, Pott disease (spinal tuberculosis), and identified chimney sweep's carcinoma as an occupational cancer.
events.sourceTitle: January 6 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Genetically Modified Pig Heart Transplanted into a Human
events.summary: Surgeons at the University of Maryland Medical Center performed the first successful transplant of a genetically modified pig heart into a human patient, advancing xenotransplantation.
events.sourceTitle: January 7 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Cardiologist William (Vilem) Ganz
events.summary: Slovakian-born American cardiologist William Ganz was born; he co-developed the Swan-Ganz pulmonary artery catheter in 1970 and pioneered early reperfusion therapy for myocardial infarction.
events.sourceTitle: January 7 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Psychologist Carl Rogers
events.summary: American psychologist Carl Rogers was born; he founded client-centered therapy, transforming modern psychotherapy and counseling practice.
events.sourceTitle: January 8 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Death of Cardiothoracic Surgeon Norman Rupert Barrett
events.summary: Australian-born British surgeon Norman Barrett died; he is eponymously remembered for describing Barrett's esophagus and pioneering thoracic surgical techniques.
events.sourceTitle: January 8 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Physician Hakaru Hashimoto
events.summary: Japanese physician Hakaru Hashimoto died; in 1912 he published the first description of autoimmune chronic thyroiditis, now known as Hashimoto's thyroiditis.
events.sourceTitle: January 9 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Albert Stevens (Patient CAL-1)
events.summary: American house painter Albert Stevens died after surviving more than two decades following an involuntary Manhattan Project plutonium injection, accumulating the highest known human radiation dose.
events.sourceTitle: January 9 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Ivor Lewis Introduces Esophagectomy Technique
events.summary: Surgeon Ivor Lewis delivered his Hunterian Lecture at the Royal College of Surgeons of England, introducing the two-stage surgical approach for esophageal carcinoma known as the Ivor Lewis procedure.
events.sourceTitle: January 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pathologist Ludwig Aschoff
events.summary: German physician and pathologist Karl Albert Ludwig Aschoff was born; he co-described the atrioventricular (Aschoff-Tawara) node and Aschoff bodies in rheumatic heart disease.
events.sourceTitle: January 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Human Insulin Injection Administered
events.summary: Fourteen-year-old Leonard Thompson received the first human injection of insulin at Toronto General Hospital, marking a turning point that transformed Type 1 diabetes from a fatal diagnosis into a treatable condition.
events.sourceTitle: The “miracle” discovery that reversed the diabetes death sentence - NobelPrize.org

events.title: First U.S. Surgeon General Report on Smoking and Health
events.summary: U.S. Surgeon General Luther Terry released the landmark federal report warning that cigarette smoking is a major health hazard and cause of lung cancer.
events.sourceTitle: January 11 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: First Use of Ether Anesthesia in France
events.summary: French surgeon Joseph François Malgaigne presented his first clinical trials of ether anesthesia to the Académie de Médecine, accelerating its adoption across France.
events.sourceTitle: January 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Continuous Epidural Catheter Analgesia in Childbirth
events.summary: Romanian obstetrician Eugen Bogdan Aburel presented the first description of continuous epidural catheter analgesia for labor pain.
events.sourceTitle: January 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Lumbar Epidural Catheter Technique Reported
events.summary: In Havana, Manuel Martínez Curbelo reported the first lumbar epidural catheter technique for continuous segmental anesthesia using a ureteral catheter threaded through a Tuohy needle.
events.sourceTitle: January 13 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Confirmed COVID-19 Case Outside China
events.summary: Thailand's Ministry of Public Health reported the first laboratory-confirmed case of novel coronavirus (SARS-CoV-2) outside China in a traveler from Wuhan.
events.sourceTitle: January 13 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Recorded Successful Cesarean Section in the United States
events.summary: Physician Jesse Bennett performed the first recorded successful cesarean section in the United States on his wife, Elizabeth Bennett, with both mother and infant surviving.
events.sourceTitle: January 14 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Surgeon François Gigot de La Peyronie
events.summary: French surgeon François Gigot de La Peyronie was born; he later described Peyronie's disease in 1743 and helped establish surgical education in France.
events.sourceTitle: January 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Trauma Surgeon Lorenz Böhler
events.summary: Austrian surgeon Lorenz Böhler was born; he pioneered modern trauma care and defined Böhler's angle for evaluating calcaneal fractures.
events.sourceTitle: January 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Percutaneous Transluminal Angioplasty Performed
events.summary: Radiologists Charles T. Dotter and Melvin Judkins performed the first intentional percutaneous transluminal angioplasty on an 82-year-old patient's femoral artery, launching interventional radiology.
events.sourceTitle: January 16 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Anatomist Antonio Maria Valsalva
events.summary: Italian anatomist Antonio Maria Valsalva was born; his studies of the ear and cardiovascular physiology led to the eponymous Valsalva maneuver.
events.sourceTitle: January 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nazi Eighth Decree Bars Jewish Dentists, Veterinarians, and Pharmacists
events.summary: Germany issued the Eighth Decree on the Reich Citizenship Law, revoking the licenses of Jewish dentists, veterinarians, and pharmacists and setting an expiration date for Jewish physicians.
events.sourceTitle: January 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Isolation of Legionella pneumophila Announced
events.summary: The CDC and microbiologist Joseph McDade announced the isolation of the bacterium later named Legionella pneumophila, identifying the cause of the 1976 Philadelphia Legionnaires' disease outbreak.
events.sourceTitle: January 18 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Use of the Zavanelli Maneuver for Shoulder Dystocia
events.summary: Obstetrician William Zavanelli performed a novel cephalic replacement and cesarean delivery to resolve an intractable shoulder dystocia, now known as the Zavanelli maneuver.
events.sourceTitle: January 18 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Sir James Young Simpson First Uses Ether in Labor
events.summary: Scottish obstetrician Sir James Young Simpson administered ether anesthesia during childbirth for the first time, before later introducing chloroform for obstetric analgesia.
events.sourceTitle: January 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: CDC Confirms First U.S. Case of COVID-19
events.summary: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention confirmed the first laboratory-proven case of SARS-CoV-2 in the United States in a patient in Snohomish County, Washington.
events.sourceTitle: January 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Russian Neurologist Vladimir Bekhterev
events.summary: Russian neurologist Vladimir Mikhailovich Bekhterev was born; he identified the role of the hippocampus in memory and described ankylosing spondylitis (Bekhterew disease).
events.sourceTitle: January 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Medical Treatise Printed in North America
events.summary: Reverend Thomas Thacher published 'A brief rule to guide the common-people of New-England how to order themselves and theirs in the Small pocks, or Measels' in Boston.
events.sourceTitle: January 21 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Nobel Laureate Camillo Golgi
events.summary: Italian pathologist Camillo Golgi died; he shared the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Santiago Ramón y Cajal and discovered the Golgi apparatus.
events.sourceTitle: January 21 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Dr. Roberta Bondar Becomes First Neurologist in Space
events.summary: Canadian neurologist Roberta Bondar launched aboard Space Shuttle Discovery (STS-42) to study how microgravity affects motion sickness, balance, and cerebral blood flow.
events.sourceTitle: January 22 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Psychiatrist Sergei Korsakoff
events.summary: Russian neuropsychiatrist Sergei Sergeievich Korsakoff was born; he later described the amnestic disorder associated with thiamine deficiency known as Korsakoff syndrome.
events.sourceTitle: January 22 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Elizabeth Blackwell Earns First U.S. Medical Degree Awarded to a Woman
events.summary: Elizabeth Blackwell graduated at the head of her class from Geneva Medical College in New York, becoming the first woman in the United States to receive a Doctor of Medicine degree.
events.sourceTitle: Geneva Medical College - Wikipedia

events.title: First Successful Refined Insulin Treatment in a Human
events.summary: At Toronto General Hospital, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson received a purified insulin injection prepared by James Collip, successfully reversing his diabetic ketoacidosis.
events.sourceTitle: January 1922 - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Otologist Heinrich Adolf Rinne
events.summary: German otologist Heinrich Adolf Rinne was born; he developed the Rinne tuning-fork test to differentiate conductive from sensorineural hearing loss.
events.sourceTitle: January 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Swiss Surgeon Fritz de Quervain
events.summary: Swiss surgeon Fritz de Quervain died; he described both de Quervain tenosynovitis of the wrist and subacute granulomatous thyroiditis.
events.sourceTitle: January 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Cesarean Section Under General Anesthesia
events.summary: Surgeon Frederic Skey performed the first cesarean section under general ether anesthesia at St Bartholomew's Hospital in London, with the infant surviving the procedure.
events.sourceTitle: January 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Dr. Janet G. Travell Appointed First Female Presidential Physician
events.summary: U.S. President John F. Kennedy appointed myofascial pain specialist Dr. Janet G. Travell as his personal physician, making her the first woman in history to hold the role.
events.sourceTitle: January 26 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Epidural Pioneer Fidel Pagés Miravé
events.summary: Spanish military surgeon Fidel Pagés Miravé was born; in 1921 he published a landmark paper describing lumbar epidural anesthesia ('anestesia metamérica').
events.sourceTitle: January 26 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Physician Thomas Willis
events.summary: English physician Thomas Willis was born; he coined the term 'neurology' and described the arterial anastomotic ring at the base of the brain known as the Circle of Willis.
events.sourceTitle: January 27 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Neurologist Carl Westphal
events.summary: German neurologist Carl Friedrich Otto Westphal died; he described the deep tendon reflex sign (Westphal sign) and co-described the Edinger-Westphal nucleus.
events.sourceTitle: January 27 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Reported Fatality Under Chloroform Anesthesia
events.summary: Fifteen-year-old Hannah Greener died during a minor toenail procedure under chloroform anesthesia in England, prompting the first systematic investigations into anesthetic safety.
events.sourceTitle: January 28 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: UK General Medical Council Rules Against Andrew Wakefield
events.summary: The UK General Medical Council delivered disciplinary findings against Andrew Wakefield regarding ethical violations in his retracted 1998 Lancet paper linking the MMR vaccine to autism.
events.sourceTitle: January 28 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Nobel Laureate Linda B. Buck
events.summary: American biologist Linda B. Buck was born; she shared the 2004 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Richard Axel for discovering odorant receptors and the organization of the olfactory system.
events.sourceTitle: Linda B. Buck - Wikipedia

events.title: Destruction of the Anatomical Theatre of the Archiginnasio
events.summary: During a World War II air raid on Bologna, Italy, the historic 17th-century Anatomical Theatre of the Archiginnasio was destroyed before later being reconstructed.
events.sourceTitle: January 29 - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Physician Robert Bentley Todd
events.summary: Irish physician Robert Bentley Todd died; he described postictal Todd's palsy and pioneered the electrical theory of epilepsy in 1849.
events.sourceTitle: January 30 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Anesthesia Pioneer Arthur Georg Läwen
events.summary: German surgeon Arthur Georg Läwen died; he pioneered paravertebral nerve blocks, sacral anesthesia, and early clinical use of curare and artificial ventilation.
events.sourceTitle: January 30 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: London Lock Hospital Opens First Venereal Disease Clinic
events.summary: Founded by surgeon William Bromfeild, the London Lock Hospital opened at Grosvenor Place as the first voluntary hospital and clinic dedicated to treating venereal diseases.
events.sourceTitle: London Lock Hospital - Wikipedia

events.title: First Reported Death Under Nitrous Oxide Anesthesia
events.summary: The first documented fatality associated with nitrous oxide anesthetic administration was recorded, spurring safer airway and gas-delivery standards.
events.sourceTitle: February 1 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Holter Monitor Inventor Norman Jefferis Holter
events.summary: American biophysicist Norman Jefferis Holter was born; in 1947 he invented the portable Holter monitor for continuous ambulatory electrocardiography.
events.sourceTitle: February 1 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Anesthesiologist Edward Boyce Tuohy
events.summary: American anesthesiologist Edward Boyce Tuohy died; he introduced the curved-tip Tuohy needle, which became standard for continuous epidural catheter placement.
events.sourceTitle: February 2 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Burn Care Pioneer Newton Clarence Browder
events.summary: American physician Newton Clarence Browder died; he co-created the Lund and Browder chart in 1942 for accurately estimating total body surface area in burn patients.
events.sourceTitle: February 2 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Recorded Pylorotomy for Infantile Pyloric Stenosis
events.summary: Scottish surgeon Sir Harold Stiles performed the first recorded pylorotomy for hypertrophic pyloric stenosis at the Royal Hospital for Sick Children in Edinburgh.
events.sourceTitle: February 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pioneer Physician Elizabeth Blackwell
events.summary: English-born physician Elizabeth Blackwell was born; she became the first woman to graduate from a medical school in the United States and a champion for women's medical education.
events.sourceTitle: February 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: World Cancer Day Established in Paris
events.summary: World Cancer Day was established at the World Summit Against Cancer for the New Millennium in Paris to unite global efforts in cancer prevention, detection, and treatment.
events.sourceTitle: February 4 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Obstetrician Adolphe Pinard
events.summary: French obstetrician Adolphe Pinard was born; he invented the Pinard fetal stethoscope (Pinard horn) in 1895 and advanced prenatal obstetric palpation.
events.sourceTitle: February 4 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Hospital Application of Caudal Epidural Anesthesia
events.summary: French urologist Fernand Léon Cathelin first applied caudal sacral epidural access in hospital practice, injecting dilute cocaine for surgical analgesia including hernia repair.
events.sourceTitle: February 5 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Anatomist Sir Arthur Keith
events.summary: Scottish anatomist Sir Arthur Keith was born; together with Martin Flack, he discovered the sinoatrial (Keith-Flack) node in 1907, explaining the heart's natural pacemaker.
events.sourceTitle: February 5 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Successful Use of Charcoal as a Poison Antidote in Humans
events.summary: French physician Charles Alexandre Hippolyte Amable Bertrand demonstrated that charcoal could successfully treat acute poisoning in humans by testing it on himself.
events.sourceTitle: February 6 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pediatrician Tomisaku Kawasaki
events.summary: Japanese pediatrician Tomisaku Kawasaki was born; he first described the childhood mucocutaneous lymph node vasculitis now known as Kawasaki disease.
events.sourceTitle: February 7 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Cardiologist Harold 'Jeremy' Swan
events.summary: Irish-born cardiologist Harold James Charles Swan died; he co-invented the flow-directed Swan-Ganz pulmonary artery catheter for hemodynamic monitoring in critical care.
events.sourceTitle: February 7 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of French Surgeon Baron Guillaume Dupuytren
events.summary: French surgeon Baron Guillaume Dupuytren died; he is remembered for describing Dupuytren contracture of the hand, Dupuytren ankle fracture, and a burn classification system.
events.sourceTitle: February 8 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Otolaryngologist John McNaughton Epley
events.summary: American otolaryngologist John McNaughton Epley was born; he developed the Epley canalith repositioning maneuver in 1980 to treat benign paroxysmal positional vertigo.
events.sourceTitle: February 8 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pathologist Howard Taylor Ricketts
events.summary: American pathologist Howard Taylor Ricketts was born; he discovered the causative bacteria of Rocky Mountain spotted fever and epidemic typhus, giving his name to the genus Rickettsia.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 9 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Nobel Laureate Jacques Monod
events.summary: French biochemist Jacques Monod was born; he shared the 1965 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning genetic control of enzyme and virus synthesis.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 9 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of French Physiologist Claude Bernard
events.summary: French physician and physiologist Claude Bernard died; he introduced the concept of the 'milieu intérieur' (internal environment), laying the foundation for modern homeostasis.
events.sourceTitle: February 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of X-Ray Discoverer Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen
events.summary: German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen died; his 1895 discovery of X-rays revolutionized diagnostic medicine and earned him the first Nobel Prize in Physics.
events.sourceTitle: February 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: BBC Airs First Live Televised Surgery Series
events.summary: The BBC broadcast the first episode of 'Your Life in Their Hands,' presented by physician Charles Fletcher, televising live hospital operations to demystify modern surgery for the public.
events.sourceTitle: February 11 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Pediatrician Antoine Marfan
events.summary: French pediatrician Antoine Bernard-Jean Marfan died; in 1896 he described the connective tissue disorder now known as Marfan syndrome.
events.sourceTitle: February 11 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of English Surgeon Sir Astley Paston Cooper
events.summary: English surgeon Sir Astley Paston Cooper died; he made pioneering contributions to vascular surgery, hernia repair, and early descriptions of major fractures and dislocations.
events.sourceTitle: February 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Obstetrician Walter Stoeckel
events.summary: German obstetrician-gynecologist Walter Stoeckel died; in 1909 he introduced caudal epidural analgesia for pain relief during labor.
events.sourceTitle: February 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Macintosh Curved Laryngoscope Described in The Lancet
events.summary: Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh published the description of his curved laryngoscope blade in The Lancet, formalizing placement of the blade tip in the vallecula for endotracheal intubation.
events.sourceTitle: February 13 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Great Ormond Street Hospital Opens in London
events.summary: Founded by Dr. Charles West with 10 beds, Great Ormond Street Hospital opened as the first hospital in the United Kingdom dedicated to inpatient care for children.
events.sourceTitle: February 14 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Edward Shenton Describes Shenton's Line of the Hip
events.summary: Guy's Hospital radiographer Edward W. H. Shenton presented a diagnostic radiographic arc of the hip joint—now known as Shenton's line—to the British Electrotherapeutic Society.
events.sourceTitle: February 14 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: George Huntington Presents 'On Chorea'
events.summary: At age 22, physician George Huntington presented his classic paper 'On Chorea' in Middleport, Ohio, providing the definitive clinical description of Huntington's disease.
events.sourceTitle: February 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Evan O'Neill Kane Performs Self-Appendectomy
events.summary: Pennsylvania surgeon Evan O'Neill Kane performed an appendectomy on himself under local anesthesia at Kane Summit Hospital to demonstrate the viability of local anesthesia.
events.sourceTitle: February 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Cardiologist and Defibrillator Pioneer Bernard Lown
events.summary: American cardiologist Bernard Lown died; he developed the direct-current (DC) defibrillator and cardioverter in 1961 and co-described Lown-Ganong-Levine syndrome.
events.sourceTitle: February 16 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: India's First Human Heart Transplant
events.summary: Cardiothoracic surgeon Prafulla Kumar Sen and his surgical team performed India's first human heart transplant, making it the sixth such procedure worldwide.
events.sourceTitle: Evolution of heart transplantation since Barnard's first - PMC

events.title: International Committee of the Red Cross Founded
events.summary: The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was founded in Geneva to improve battlefield medical care and establish international humanitarian protections for the wounded.
events.sourceTitle: February 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Stethoscope Inventor René Laennec
events.summary: French physician René-Théophile-Hyacinthe Laennec was born; he invented the stethoscope in 1816 and coined the medical terms cirrhosis and melanoma.
events.sourceTitle: February 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Physiologist Marshall Hall
events.summary: English physician Marshall Hall was born; he pioneered understanding of the spinal reflex arc and introduced the 'Ready Method' of artificial respiration for asphyxia.
events.sourceTitle: February 18 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Pediatrician Hans Asperger
events.summary: Austrian pediatrician Hans Asperger was born; he described a distinct pattern of neurodevelopmental traits later termed Asperger syndrome.
events.sourceTitle: February 18 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Nobel Laureate André Frédéric Cournand
events.summary: French-born physician André Frédéric Cournand died; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for pioneering human cardiac catheterization.
events.sourceTitle: February 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Ophthalmologist Herman Snellen Sr.
events.summary: Dutch ophthalmologist Herman Snellen Sr. was born; in 1862 he introduced the Snellen eye chart and optotypes for standardized visual acuity testing.
events.sourceTitle: February 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: University of California Establishes Medical Department (Future UCSF)
events.summary: The Regents of the University of California assumed control of Toland Medical College to form the UC Medical Department—later UCSF—and resolved to admit women students.
events.sourceTitle: February 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Dermatologist Hulusi Behçet
events.summary: Turkish dermatologist Hulusi Behçet was born; in 1937 he described the multisystem inflammatory vasculitis now known as Behçet's disease.
events.sourceTitle: February 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Vitamin K Discoverer Henrik Dam
events.summary: Danish biochemist Henrik Dam was born; he won the 1943 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering vitamin K and its essential role in blood coagulation.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 21 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Interventional Radiology Pioneer Sven-Ivar Seldinger
events.summary: Swedish radiologist Sven-Ivar Seldinger died; in 1953 he introduced the Seldinger wire-guided technique for safe percutaneous access to blood vessels and hollow organs.
events.sourceTitle: February 21 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Cloning of Dolly the Sheep Announced
events.summary: Scientists at the Roslin Institute in Scotland announced the successful cloning of Dolly the sheep from an adult somatic cell, transforming genetics and stem cell research.
events.sourceTitle: February 22 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Nobel Laureate Virologist Renato Dulbecco
events.summary: Italian-born American virologist Renato Dulbecco was born; he shared the 1975 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries on how tumor viruses interact with cellular DNA.
events.sourceTitle: February 22 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of CT Scan Co-Inventor Allan MacLeod Cormack
events.summary: South African-American physicist Allan MacLeod Cormack was born; he shared the 1979 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing X-ray computed tomography (CT) scanning.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 23 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Surgeon Alberto Gutiérrez
events.summary: Argentine surgeon Alberto Gutiérrez died; in 1933 he introduced the 'hanging drop' sign for identifying the epidural space during regional anesthesia.
events.sourceTitle: February 23 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Tumor Angiogenesis Pioneer Judah Folkman
events.summary: American medical scientist Judah Folkman was born; he founded the field of tumor angiogenesis research, showing how tumors recruit blood vessels and inspiring anti-angiogenic cancer therapies.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 24 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Anatomical Pathology Founder Giovanni Battista Morgagni
events.summary: Italian physician Giovanni Battista Morgagni was born; his 1761 work correlated postmortem findings with clinical symptoms, establishing modern anatomical pathology.
events.sourceTitle: February 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Orthopedic Surgeon Riccardo Galeazzi
events.summary: Italian orthopedic surgeon Riccardo Galeazzi died; he described the Galeazzi forearm fracture-dislocation in 1934 and the Galeazzi test for hip dislocation.
events.sourceTitle: February 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Televised Kidney Transplant
events.summary: The first televised kidney transplant was broadcast on television's Today Show, bringing organ transplantation surgery into public view.
events.sourceTitle: February 26 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Death of Pioneer Physician Anandibai Gopal Joshi
events.summary: Anandibai Gopal Joshi, the first Indian woman educated in Western medicine in the United States, died of tuberculosis at age 21.
events.sourceTitle: February 26 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Insulin Co-Discoverer Charles Best
events.summary: Canadian medical scientist Charles Herbert Best was born; as Frederick Banting's research assistant in 1921, he played a central role in isolating insulin for diabetes treatment.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - February 27 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Cortisone Co-Discoverer Philip Showalter Hench
