events.title: Birth of Rudolph Matas, Father of Vascular Surgery
events.summary: American surgeon Rudolph Matas was born; he pioneered endoaneurysmorrhaphy and spinal anesthesia techniques, earning recognition as the father of vascular surgery.
events.sourceTitle: September 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Phineas Gage Survives Severe Frontal Lobe Tamping Iron Injury
events.summary: Railroad foreman Phineas Gage survived an explosion that drove an iron rod through his skull and left frontal lobe, becoming a landmark case in understanding brain localization and personality.
events.sourceTitle: Phineas Gage - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Walter Reed, Yellow Fever Researcher
events.summary: U.S. Army physician Walter Reed was born; in 1901 he led the team that confirmed Carlos Finlay's theory that yellow fever is transmitted by mosquitoes.
events.sourceTitle: Walter Reed - Wikipedia

events.title: First Approved Human Gene Therapy Trial Begins
events.summary: Four-year-old Ashanti DeSilva, who had ADA-SCID, received genetically modified T cells at the NIH in the world's first approved human gene therapy clinical trial.
events.sourceTitle: The First Human Gene Therapy | Biomol Blog

events.title: Birth of Ferid Murad, Nitric Oxide Signaling Nobel Laureate
events.summary: American physician and pharmacologist Ferid Murad was born; he shared the 1998 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that nitroglycerin acts by releasing nitric oxide to relax smooth muscle.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 14 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: First Public Presentation of Local Anesthesia Using Cocaine
events.summary: At the German Ophthalmological Society congress in Heidelberg, Josef Brettauer presented Carl Koller's experiments demonstrating cocaine's efficacy as a topical local anesthetic for eye surgery.
events.sourceTitle: September 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Luther Terry, U.S. Surgeon General Who Warned on Tobacco
events.summary: American physician Luther Terry was born; as the ninth U.S. Surgeon General, he issued the landmark 1964 report linking cigarette smoking to lung cancer and heart disease.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 15 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Albrecht Kossel, Nucleic Acid Nobel Laureate
events.summary: German biochemist Albrecht Kossel was born; he won the 1910 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for determining the chemical composition of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA).
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 16 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Sir Thomas Lauder Brunton, Nitrate Therapy Pioneer
events.summary: Scottish physician Sir Thomas Lauder Brunton died; he introduced amyl nitrite in 1867 for the relief of angina pectoris, laying the foundation for nitrate therapy in cardiology.
events.sourceTitle: September 16 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Inaugural WHO World Patient Safety Day
events.summary: Following its adoption by the World Health Assembly in 2019, the World Health Organization established September 17 as World Patient Safety Day to reduce preventable harm in healthcare.
events.sourceTitle: WORLD PATIENT SAFETY DAY - National Day Calendar

events.title: Death of Henrik Sjögren, Describer of Sjögren Syndrome
events.summary: Swedish ophthalmologist Henrik Samuel Conrad Sjögren died; he described keratoconjunctivitis sicca (Sjögren syndrome) and introduced 1% rose bengal staining in 1933.
events.sourceTitle: September 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: World's First Mother-to-Daughter Uterus Transplant
events.summary: Surgeons at the University of Gothenburg in Sweden performed the world's first mother-to-daughter uterus transplantation, advancing reproductive transplant surgery.
events.sourceTitle: September 18 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Uğur Şahin, Co-Developer of mRNA COVID-19 Vaccine
events.summary: German immunologist and BioNTech co-founder Uğur Şahin was born; his research led to the first authorized mRNA-based vaccine for COVID-19.
events.sourceTitle: September 18 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: James Leonard Corning Publishes Regional Anesthesia Technique
events.summary: American neurologist James Leonard Corning published an experimental method in the New York Medical Journal to prolong regional anesthesia by restricting blood flow to prolong cocaine's neural action.
events.sourceTitle: September 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Irving Freiler Stein, Co-Describer of PCOS
events.summary: American gynecologist Irving Freiler Stein was born; he co-described Stein-Leventhal syndrome—now known as polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS)—in 1934.
events.sourceTitle: September 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Luigi Galvani Records Pivotal 'Animal Electricity' Observation
events.summary: Italian physician and anatomist Luigi Galvani observed a dissected frog's leg muscle contract when its nerve was touched by a metal scalpel near an electrical machine, founding electrophysiology.
events.sourceTitle: September 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Ernest William Goodpasture, Pathologist
events.summary: American pathologist Ernest William Goodpasture died; he described Goodpasture syndrome in 1919 and pioneered viral cultivation in chick embryos for vaccine production.
events.sourceTitle: September 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Charles Nicolle, Discoverer of Typhus Transmission
events.summary: French bacteriologist Charles Nicolle was born; he won the 1928 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that body lice transmit epidemic typhus.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 21 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Fidel Pagés, Pioneer of Epidural Anesthesia
events.summary: Spanish military surgeon Fidel Pagés Miravé died; his landmark 1921 paper introduced 'anestesia metamérica,' the first clinical description of lumbar epidural anesthesia.
events.sourceTitle: September 21 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Dorothy Reed Mendenhall, Co-Describer of Reed-Sternberg Cells
events.summary: American physician Dorothy Reed was born; in 1902 she characterized the giant multinucleated cells (Reed-Sternberg cells) diagnostic of Hodgkin lymphoma.
events.sourceTitle: September 22 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of John W. Lachman, Developer of the Lachman Test
events.summary: American orthopedic surgeon John W. Lachman was born; he devised the Lachman test (1976), the gold-standard physical exam maneuver for anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) injury.
events.sourceTitle: September 22 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Josef Jadassohn Presents Patch Testing for Contact Dermatitis
events.summary: German dermatologist Josef Jadassohn presented his findings on eczematous skin reactions to mercurial compounds at the 5th Congress of the German Society of Dermatology, establishing diagnostic patch testing.
events.sourceTitle: September 23 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Hermann Boerhaave, Pioneer of Clinical Teaching
events.summary: Dutch physician Hermann Boerhaave died; he pioneered bedside clinical instruction in Leiden and first described spontaneous esophageal rupture (Boerhaave syndrome) in 1724.
events.sourceTitle: September 23 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Jerome W. Conn, Describer of Conn Syndrome
events.summary: American endocrinologist Jerome W. Conn was born; in 1955 he described primary hyperaldosteronism (Conn syndrome) and helped elucidate the renin-angiotensin-aldosterone axis.
events.sourceTitle: September 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of André Frédéric Cournand, Cardiac Catheterization Nobel Laureate
events.summary: French-born American physician André Frédéric Cournand died; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing cardiac catheterization.
events.sourceTitle: September 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Carl Wunderlich, Pioneer of Clinical Thermometry
events.summary: German physician Carl Reinhold August Wunderlich died; his 1868 treatise established 37 °C (98.6 °F) as normal human body temperature and introduced routine clinical thermometry.
events.sourceTitle: September 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Werner Forssmann, Pioneer of Cardiac Catheterization
events.summary: German physician Werner Forssmann died; in 1929 he performed the first human cardiac catheterization on himself, earning a share of the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
events.sourceTitle: September 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Ivan Pavlov, Pioneer of Classical Conditioning
events.summary: Russian physiologist Ivan Pavlov was born; he won the 1904 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his research on digestive physiology and classical conditioning.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 26 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Ugo Cerletti, Co-Developer of Electroconvulsive Therapy
events.summary: Italian neuropsychiatrist Ugo Cerletti was born; in 1938 he and Lucio Bini introduced electroconvulsive therapy (ECT) for severe psychiatric disorders.
events.sourceTitle: September 26 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Measles Certified Eliminated from the Americas
events.summary: The Pan American Health Organization and World Health Organization certified the Region of the Americas free of endemic measles, marking a historic vaccination milestone.
events.sourceTitle: Vaccine Timeline Before Jenner and After COVID-19

events.title: Mary Toft Medical Hoax Investigation Begins
events.summary: Mary Toft of Surrey, England, was reported to have delivered animal parts, prompting an investigation by leading London physicians including obstetrician James Douglas, who exposed the fraud.
events.sourceTitle: September 27 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Alexander Fleming Discovers Penicillin
events.summary: Scottish bacteriologist Alexander Fleming observed that a Penicillium mold contaminating a Staphylococcus culture plate lysed surrounding bacteria, ushering in the antibiotic era.
events.sourceTitle: September 28 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Louis Pasteur, Father of Microbiology and Immunology
events.summary: French chemist and microbiologist Louis Pasteur died; his discoveries of germ theory, pasteurization, and vaccines against anthrax and rabies transformed medicine. World Rabies Day is observed on this date.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 28 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Willem Einthoven, Inventor of the Electrocardiogram
events.summary: Dutch physician and physiologist Willem Einthoven died; he developed the first practical string galvanometer electrocardiogram (ECG) in 1903 and won the 1924 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
events.sourceTitle: September 29 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of François Dessertenne, Describer of Torsades de Pointes
events.summary: French cardiologist François Dessertenne was born; in 1966 he first described and named the polymorphic ventricular tachycardia known as torsades de pointes.
events.sourceTitle: September 29 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Barry Marshall, Co-Discoverer of Helicobacter pylori
events.summary: Australian physician Barry J. Marshall was born; he and Robin Warren proved that Helicobacter pylori causes most peptic ulcers, earning the 2005 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - September 30 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Robert Arden Miller, Designer of the Miller Laryngoscope Blade
events.summary: American anesthesiologist Robert Arden Miller died; in 1941 he designed the straight Miller laryngoscope blade, which remains a standard tool for endotracheal intubation.
events.sourceTitle: September 30 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded to James Allison and Tasuku Honjo for Cancer Immunotherapy
events.summary: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to James P. Allison and Tasuku Honjo for discovering cancer therapy by inhibition of negative immune regulation (checkpoint inhibitors).
events.sourceTitle: Compound Interest: The 2018 Nobel Prize in Physiology/Medicine

events.title: Birth of William Stokes, Pioneer of Thoracic Auscultation
events.summary: Irish physician William Stokes was born; he promoted percussion and auscultation and co-described Stokes-Adams syndrome (1846) and Cheyne-Stokes respiration (1854).
events.sourceTitle: October 1 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for mRNA Vaccines
events.summary: The Nobel Assembly awarded the 2023 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine to Katalin Karikó and Drew Weissman for discoveries concerning nucleoside base modifications that enabled effective mRNA vaccines against COVID-19.
events.sourceTitle: Katalin Karikó - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Berkeley Moynihan, Pioneer of Abdominal Surgery
events.summary: English surgeon Berkeley George Andrew Moynihan was born; he advanced abdominal and hepatobiliary surgery and described Moynihan's sign and Moynihan's hump of the right hepatic artery.
events.sourceTitle: October 2 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Issue of the British Medical Journal Published
events.summary: The Provincial Medical and Surgical Journal published its first issue (Vol. 1, No. 1), later adopting the title British Medical Journal (BMJ) in 1857.
events.sourceTitle: October 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded to Svante Pääbo for Paleogenomics
events.summary: Swedish geneticist Svante Pääbo won the 2022 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for sequencing the Neanderthal genome and discovering the Denisovan hominin.
events.sourceTitle: Swedish scientist Svante Paabo wins Nobel Prize in medicine - Al Jazeera

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded to David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian
events.summary: David Julius and Ardem Patapoutian were awarded the 2021 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the cellular receptors for temperature and mechanical touch.
events.sourceTitle: NAM member David Julius Receives Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

events.title: Birth of Alan L. Hart, Pioneer of Tuberculosis Radiology Screening
events.summary: American physician and radiologist Alan L. Hart was born; he pioneered the use of chest X-ray screening to detect tuberculosis early and curb its spread.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 4 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: The Lancet Publishes Its First Issue
events.summary: Founded by Thomas Wakley, The Lancet published its inaugural issue (Vol. 1, No. 1), launching a new era of independent medical journalism and healthcare reform.
events.sourceTitle: October 5 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Discovery of Hepatitis C Virus
events.summary: Harvey J. Alter, Michael Houghton, and Charles M. Rice were awarded the 2020 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for the discovery of the Hepatitis C virus.
events.sourceTitle: Dr. Michael Houghton Wins 2020 Nobel Prize | University of Alberta

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Peripheral Immune Tolerance
events.summary: Mary E. Brunkow, Frederick J. Ramsdell, and Shimon Sakaguchi were awarded the 2025 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries concerning peripheral immune tolerance and regulatory T cells.
events.sourceTitle: Press release: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2025

events.title: Birth of Wilhelm von Waldeyer-Hartz, Coiner of 'Neuron' and 'Chromosome'
events.summary: German anatomist Wilhelm Gottfried Waldeyer-Hartz was born; he described Waldeyer's tonsillar ring (1884) and popularized the neuron theory.
events.sourceTitle: October 6 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Jules Tinel Publishes Description of Tinel's Sign
events.summary: French neurologist Jules Tinel published 'Le signe du fourmillement dans les lésions des nerfs périphériques,' describing distal tingling elicited by percussing an injured peripheral nerve.
events.sourceTitle: October 7 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Nobel Prize Awarded for Cellular Oxygen Sensing
events.summary: William G. Kaelin Jr., Sir Peter J. Ratcliffe, and Gregg L. Semenza were awarded the 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering how cells sense and adapt to oxygen availability.
events.sourceTitle: NIH grantees win 2019 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine

events.title: Death of Sir Henry Head, Pioneer of Sensory Neuroanatomy
events.summary: English neurologist Sir Henry Head died; he mapped human dermatomes, characterized visceral referred pain (Head's zones), and co-described autonomic dysreflexia (Head-Riddoch syndrome).
events.sourceTitle: October 8 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of George Henry Fox, Co-Describer of Fox-Fordyce Disease
events.summary: American dermatologist George Henry Fox was born; he was a pioneer of dermatologic photography and co-described Fox-Fordyce disease in 1902.
events.sourceTitle: October 8 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Ralph Milton Waters, Founder of Academic Anesthesiology
events.summary: American anesthesiologist Ralph Milton Waters was born; he founded the first academic anesthesiology program at the University of Wisconsin and invented the Waters CO2 absorption canister.
events.sourceTitle: October 9 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Gabriele Falloppio, Discoverer of the Fallopian Tubes
events.summary: Italian anatomist and physician Gabriele Falloppio died; he provided the first accurate anatomical description of the uterine (Fallopian) tubes and several cranial nerves.
events.sourceTitle: October 9 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Founding of SICOT, International Orthopedic Surgery Society
events.summary: An international group of orthopedic surgeons met at the Hôtel Crillon in Paris to found SICOT (Société Internationale de Chirurgie Orthopédique et de Traumatologie).
events.sourceTitle: October 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Octave Landry, First Describer of Guillain-Barré Syndrome
events.summary: French physician Jean-Baptiste Octave Landry de Thézillat was born; in 1859 he published the first clinical description of acute ascending paralysis, later known as Guillain-Barré syndrome.
events.sourceTitle: October 10 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of John Hilton Edwards, Describer of Trisomy 18
events.summary: English geneticist John Hilton Edwards died; in 1960 he first described Trisomy 18 (Edwards syndrome), a major chromosomal disorder.
events.sourceTitle: October 11 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Irving Freiler Stein, Co-Describer of PCOS
events.summary: American gynecologist Irving Freiler Stein died; alongside Michael Leventhal, he characterized polycystic ovary syndrome (Stein-Leventhal syndrome) in 1934.
events.sourceTitle: October 11 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Clinical Use of the Iron Lung Respirator
events.summary: The Drinker-Shaw negative-pressure iron lung respirator was used for the first time at Boston Children's Hospital to support a young girl with respiratory paralysis from polio.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 12 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of René Leriche, Pioneer of Vascular Surgery
events.summary: French surgeon Henri Marie René Leriche was born; he described aortoiliac occlusive disease (Leriche syndrome) in 1940 and advanced sympathectomy and vascular surgery.
events.sourceTitle: October 12 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: CDC Obtains First Electron Micrograph of Ebola Virus
events.summary: Researchers at the U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) obtained the first electron micrograph of an Ebola viral particle during the initial 1976 outbreak.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 13 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Rudolf Virchow, Founder of Cellular Pathology
events.summary: German physician and pathologist Rudolf Virchow was born in Schivelbein; he revolutionized pathology by demonstrating that diseases arise from abnormalities within individual cells.
events.sourceTitle: Rudolf Virchow | Biography, Discovery, & Facts - Britannica

events.title: Birth of C. Everett Koop, 13th U.S. Surgeon General
events.summary: American pediatric surgeon and public health leader Charles Everett Koop was born; as U.S. Surgeon General (1982–1989), he led major public health campaigns on HIV/AIDS and tobacco.
events.sourceTitle: October 14 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Armand Trousseau, Master Clinician
events.summary: French physician Armand Trousseau was born; he described Trousseau's sign of latent tetany (1861) and Trousseau's syndrome of migratory thrombophlebitis associated with occult malignancy.
events.sourceTitle: October 14 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Global Handwashing Day Launched
events.summary: The Global Public-Private Partnership for Handwashing launched the inaugural Global Handwashing Day to promote handwashing with soap as an effective, low-cost intervention against infectious diseases.
events.sourceTitle: October 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Augusta Déjerine-Klumpke, Neuroanatomy Pioneer
events.summary: American-born French neurologist Augusta Déjerine-Klumpke was born; she described lower brachial plexus palsy (Klumpke's palsy) in 1885 and co-authored landmark neuroanatomy texts.
events.sourceTitle: October 15 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Public Demonstration of Surgical Ether Anesthesia ('Ether Day')
events.summary: Dentist William T. G. Morton administered diethyl ether to a patient while surgeon John Collins Warren excised a neck tumor at Massachusetts General Hospital, inaugurating modern surgical anesthesia.
events.sourceTitle: Celebrating the 175th Anniversary of Anesthesiology - Wood Library-Museum

events.title: Death of Santiago Ramón y Cajal, Father of Modern Neuroscience
events.summary: Spanish neuroscientist and pathologist Santiago Ramón y Cajal died; he established the neuron doctrine and won the 1906 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine.
events.sourceTitle: October 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh, Inventor of the Curved Laryngoscope
events.summary: New Zealand-born anesthetist Sir Robert Reynolds Macintosh was born; he invented the curved Macintosh laryngoscope blade in 1943 and helped establish Oxford's chair of anesthetics.
events.sourceTitle: October 17 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Alfred Binet, Creator of the First Practical Intelligence Test
events.summary: French psychologist Alfred Binet died; alongside Théodore Simon, he developed the Binet-Simon scale, the foundation of modern standardized cognitive and intelligence testing.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 18 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Philipp Franz von Siebold, Introducer of Western Medicine to Japan
events.summary: German physician and botanist Philipp Franz von Siebold died; he taught Western clinical medicine and surgery in Nagasaki, influencing modern Japanese medical practice.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 18 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Streptomycin Isolated by Rutgers University Researchers
events.summary: Researchers at Rutgers University isolated streptomycin, the first aminoglycoside antibiotic and the first effective antimicrobial treatment for tuberculosis.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 19 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Philip Drinker, Co-Inventor of the Iron Lung
events.summary: American industrial hygienist and chemical engineer Philip Drinker died; he co-invented the Drinker respirator (iron lung) in 1928 to sustain patients with polio-induced respiratory paralysis.
events.sourceTitle: October 19 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Thomas Bartholin, Discoverer of the Human Lymphatic System
events.summary: Danish physician and anatomist Thomas Bartholin was born; he published the first full description of the human lymphatic system and documented refrigeration anesthesia in 1661.
events.sourceTitle: October 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Austin Flint, Describer of the Austin Flint Murmur
events.summary: American physician Austin Flint was born; he promoted the binaural stethoscope and described the Austin Flint diastolic murmur associated with severe aortic regurgitation in 1862.
events.sourceTitle: October 20 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Oswald Avery, Pioneer Who Proved DNA Carries Genetic Information
events.summary: Canadian-born American physician and researcher Oswald Theodore Avery was born; his 1944 experiments demonstrated that DNA, rather than protein, is the transforming principle of heredity.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 21 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Caleb Hillier Parry, Early Describer of Graves' Disease
events.summary: English physician Caleb Hillier Parry was born; his posthumous 1825 papers contained early clinical descriptions of hyperthyroid goiter (Parry's disease) and Hirschsprung's disease.
events.sourceTitle: October 21 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Ralph Huber Patented the Non-Coring Hypodermic Needle Point
events.summary: Ralph Lee Huber received a U.S. patent for a curved, non-coring hypodermic needle tip ('Huber point') that prevented tissue plugging and later formed the basis of the Tuohy epidural needle.
events.sourceTitle: October 22 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Albert Szent-Györgyi, Discoverer of Vitamin C
events.summary: Hungarian biochemist Albert Szent-Györgyi died; he won the 1937 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for isolating vitamin C (ascorbic acid) and elucidating biological oxidation.
events.sourceTitle: October 22 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Moritz Kaposi, Describer of Kaposi Sarcoma
events.summary: Hungarian dermatologist Moritz Kaposi was born; he first described idiopathic multiple pigmented sarcoma of the skin—now known as Kaposi sarcoma—in 1872.
events.sourceTitle: October 23 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Charles Clifford Macklin, Describer of the Macklin Effect
events.summary: Canadian pulmonologist Charles Clifford Macklin was born; in 1939 he explained the mechanism of alveolar rupture and air dissection leading to pneumomediastinum (the Macklin effect).
events.sourceTitle: October 23 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Antonie van Leeuwenhoek, Father of Microbiology
events.summary: Dutch microscopist Antonie van Leeuwenhoek was born; using handcrafted single-lens microscopes, he became the first person to observe and document bacteria, protozoa, and muscle fibers.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 24 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: World Polio Day Observed Globally in Honor of Jonas Salk
events.summary: Observed annually on October 24 to commemorate Jonas Salk's birthday month and mobilize global efforts by Rotary International, WHO, and UNICEF toward complete polio eradication.
events.sourceTitle: Jonas Salk - Wikipedia

events.title: Dame Averil Mansfield Appointed First Female Professor of Surgery in the UK
events.summary: Vascular surgeon Dame Averil Mansfield became the first woman appointed Professor of Surgery in the United Kingdom, marking a milestone for women in academic surgical leadership.
events.sourceTitle: October 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Harold Leeming Sheehan, Describer of Sheehan Syndrome
events.summary: English pathologist Harold Leeming Sheehan died; in 1937 he described postpartum pituitary necrosis (Sheehan syndrome) following severe obstetric hemorrhage.
events.sourceTitle: October 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Last Natural Case of Smallpox (Ali Maow Maalin)
events.summary: Hospital cook Ali Maow Maalin developed a smallpox rash in Merka, Somalia, marking the world's last naturally acquired case of variola minor and a decisive milestone toward global eradication.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 26 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Leonard Bailey Performs Baboon-to-Human Heart Transplant on 'Baby Fae'
events.summary: At Loma Linda University Medical Center, surgeon Leonard L. Bailey transplanted a baboon heart into a 12-day-old infant with hypoplastic left heart syndrome ('Baby Fae'), a landmark xenotransplantation case.
events.sourceTitle: Leonard Lee Bailey - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Michael Servetus, First European to Describe Pulmonary Circulation
events.summary: Spanish physician and theologian Michael Servetus was executed in Geneva; in his writings he became the first European to accurately describe pulmonary circulation of blood from the heart through the lungs.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 27 - Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Donora Smog Disaster Begins in Pennsylvania
events.summary: A severe industrial temperature-inversion smog trapped toxic pollutants over Donora, Pennsylvania, killing 20 people and sickening thousands, catalyzing modern U.S. air pollution and environmental health legislation.
events.sourceTitle: October 27 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Jonas Salk, Developer of the Inactivated Polio Vaccine
events.summary: American virologist Jonas Salk was born in New York City; he developed the first safe and effective inactivated polio vaccine (1955), transforming global pediatric public health.
events.sourceTitle: Jonas Salk (1914-1995): Pioneering the Fight Against Polio - PMC

events.title: Birth of Henry Koplik, Describer of Koplik Spots in Measles
events.summary: American pediatrician Henry Koplik was born; in 1896 he described the pathognomonic oral mucosal lesions (Koplik spots) that appear prior to the measles skin rash.
events.sourceTitle: October 28 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Joseph Babinski, Describer of the Babinski Reflex
events.summary: French neurologist Joseph Jules François Félix Babinski died; he discovered the plantar extensor response (Babinski sign) indicating corticospinal tract dysfunction.
events.sourceTitle: October 29 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Death of Wilhelm Heinrich Erb, Pioneer of Electrodiagnosis
events.summary: German neurologist Wilhelm Heinrich Erb died; he pioneered clinical electrotherapy and described Erb-Duchenne brachial plexus palsy and limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.
events.sourceTitle: October 29 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Dickinson W. Richards Jr., Cardiac Catheterization Laureate
events.summary: American physician Dickinson Woodruff Richards Jr. was born; he shared the 1956 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with André Cournand and Werner Forssmann for developing cardiac catheterization.
events.sourceTitle: October 30 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: U.S. National Doctors' Day Signed into Federal Law
events.summary: President George H. W. Bush signed legislation designating March 30 as U.S. National Doctors' Day to honor physicians and commemorate the first surgical use of ether anesthesia in 1842.
events.sourceTitle: March 30 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Adolf von Baeyer, Organic Chemist and Barbituric Acid Pioneer
events.summary: German chemist Adolf von Baeyer was born; his synthesis of barbituric acid and organic ring structures laid the groundwork for barbiturate sedatives and modern medicinal chemistry.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 31 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Paolo Mantegazza, Early Researcher of Cocaine's Physiological Effects
events.summary: Italian neurologist and physiologist Paolo Mantegazza was born; in 1859 he published early experimental observations on the physiological and neuropsychiatric effects of coca leaves.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - October 31 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: First Medical School for Women Opens in Boston
events.summary: The New England Female Medical College opened in Boston as the first medical school dedicated to women. It later merged with Boston University in 1874 to become one of the world's first co-educational medical schools.
events.sourceTitle: November - National Women's History Alliance

events.title: NIH Establishes National Microbiological Institute
events.summary: The National Institutes of Health established the National Microbiological Institute (precursor to NIAID) and the Experimental Biology and Medicine Institute, incorporating the Rocky Mountain Laboratory and Biologics Control Laboratory.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Dieulafoy Subcutaneous Aspirator Presented
events.summary: Georges-Paul Dieulafoy's piston-driven subcutaneous aspirator with interchangeable trocars and cannulae was presented to the Académie de Médecine in Paris. It introduced a safer, less invasive method for draining pleural effusions and deep fluid collections.
events.sourceTitle: November 2 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: CDC Recommends Pediatric COVID-19 Vaccine for Ages 5–11
events.summary: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control and Prevention's Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices (ACIP) recommended the Pfizer-BioNTech pediatric COVID-19 vaccine for all children ages 5 to 11 years.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Vitamin K Discoverer Edward Adelbert Doisy
events.summary: American biochemist Edward Adelbert Doisy was born in Hume, Illinois. He shared the 1943 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the chemical nature of vitamin K, essential for blood coagulation.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Diphtheria Antitoxin Pioneer Émile Roux
events.summary: French physician and bacteriologist Émile Roux, a close collaborator of Louis Pasteur and co-founder of the Pasteur Institute, died in Paris. He co-developed the first effective serum therapy (antitoxin) against diphtheria.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Anesthetic Properties of Chloroform Discovered
events.summary: Scottish obstetrician James Young Simpson discovered the anesthetic properties of chloroform in Edinburgh after experimenting with its inhalation alongside colleagues. Chloroform quickly became a widely used surgical and obstetric anesthetic.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History -November 4 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: NCBI and NIH Office of AIDS Research Established
events.summary: U.S. Congress established the National Center for Biotechnology Information (NCBI) within the National Library of Medicine, while President Reagan signed the HOPE Act establishing the NIH Office of AIDS Research.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Death of Vitamin Pioneer Christiaan Eijkman
events.summary: Dutch physician and pathologist Christiaan Eijkman died in Utrecht. He won the 1929 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for demonstrating that beriberi is caused by a dietary deficiency, laying the groundwork for the discovery of vitamins.
events.sourceTitle: Today in Medical History - November 5th | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: CDC Issues First Clinical Precautions for AIDS
events.summary: The U.S. Centers for Disease Control published its first set of precautions in the Morbidity and Mortality Weekly Report for clinical and laboratory staff caring for patients with signs of AIDS.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: First Activation of a Surgically Implanted Insulin Pump
events.summary: At the University of Minnesota, a 54-year-old patient with type 2 diabetes received the first activation of a surgically implanted insulin pump (Infusaid Model 400) for continuous insulin delivery.
events.sourceTitle: November 1980 - Wikipedia

events.title: Landmark Separation of Conjoined Twins in Manchester
events.summary: Surgeons in Manchester, England, performed a high-profile separation of conjoined twin girls following complex legal and bioethical review, saving one twin while the other died.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - November 06 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Radioactivity Pioneer Marie Curie
events.summary: Polish-French physicist and chemist Marie Curie was born in Warsaw. Her discovery of polonium and radium earned two Nobel Prizes and enabled the development of modern radiation therapy for cancer.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Approves First Rapid 20-Minute HIV Test
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved the first rapid diagnostic HIV blood test kit capable of delivering results with 99.6% accuracy in 20 minutes without specialized laboratory equipment.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen Discovers X-Rays
events.summary: German physicist Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen discovered X-rays while experimenting with cathode-ray tubes in Würzburg, transforming medical diagnostics by allowing non-invasive visualization of internal anatomy. November 8 is observed globally as World Radiography Day.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Surgical Pioneer Bernhard von Langenbeck
events.summary: German surgeon Bernhard von Langenbeck was born in Padingbüttel. He pioneered numerous operative techniques, including surgical residency training concepts, and founded Langenbeck's Archives of Surgery, the oldest surgical journal in the world.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - November 9 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: FDA Grants First EUA for COVID-19 Monoclonal Antibody
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Eli Lilly's bamlanivimab, the first monoclonal antibody therapy authorized to prevent progression to severe COVID-19 in high-risk patients.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: National Heart and Lung Institute Established at NIH
events.summary: The U.S. Department of Health, Education, and Welfare redesignated the National Heart Institute as the National Heart and Lung Institute (later NHLBI), expanding federal pulmonary disease research.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: CDC and WHO Report Steepest Rise in Unvaccinated Children for Measles
events.summary: CDC and WHO reported that more than 22 million infants missed their first measles vaccine dose in 2020 due to pandemic disruptions, marking the largest global increase in two decades.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Abdominal Surgery Pioneer Ephraim McDowell
events.summary: American surgeon Ephraim McDowell was born in Virginia. In 1809, he performed the world's first successful removal of an ovarian tumor without anesthesia, earning recognition as the founding father of abdominal surgery.
events.sourceTitle: Ephraim McDowell - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Evidence-Based Medicine Pioneer Gordon Guyatt
events.summary: Canadian physician Gordon Guyatt was born in Hamilton, Ontario. He coined the term 'evidence-based medicine' in 1991 and led foundational efforts to integrate clinical trial evidence into everyday medical decision-making.
events.sourceTitle: Gordon Guyatt - Wikipedia

events.title: Egas Moniz Performs First Modern Frontal Lobe Psychosurgery
events.summary: Portuguese neurologist António Egas Moniz directed the first modern prefrontal leukotomy at Santa Marta Hospital in Lisbon to treat severe psychiatric illness, work that later earned the 1949 Nobel Prize.
events.sourceTitle: November 12 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Ricky Ray Hemophilia Relief Fund Act Enacted
events.summary: U.S. Congress enacted the Ricky Ray Hemophilia Relief Fund Act, authorizing compensation for individuals with hemophilia and clotting disorders who contracted HIV from contaminated blood products between 1982 and 1987.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: University of Edinburgh Admits First Women to Medical School
events.summary: Sophia Jex-Blake and her fellow female students (the Edinburgh Seven) were admitted to study medicine at the University of Edinburgh, marking a watershed moment for women in British medical education.
events.sourceTitle: Historic Events of November - ScotClans

events.title: U.S. Supreme Court Upholds School Vaccination Mandates
events.summary: In Zucht v. King, the U.S. Supreme Court upheld the constitutional authority of school districts to exclude unvaccinated students even in the absence of an active outbreak.
events.sourceTitle: Today in Medical History- November 13th | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Insulin Co-Discoverer Sir Frederick Banting
events.summary: Canadian physician and orthopedist Frederick Banting was born in Alliston, Ontario. For co-discovering insulin in 1921, he became the youngest Nobel laureate in Physiology or Medicine in 1923; his birthday is observed as World Diabetes Day.
events.sourceTitle: Frederick Banting - Wikipedia

events.title: Inauguration of the Pasteur Institute in Paris
events.summary: Following the success of Louis Pasteur's rabies vaccine and an international fundraising campaign, the Pasteur Institute was officially inaugurated in Paris as a premier center for microbiology and vaccine research.
events.sourceTitle: Louis Pasteur - Vaccines, Microbiology, Bacteriology | Britannica

events.title: FDA Approves Valium (Diazepam)
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved Valium (diazepam), synthesized by chemist Leo Sternbach at Hoffmann-La Roche, which became the most widely prescribed medication in the world from 1969 to 1982.
events.sourceTitle: November 15 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: Pakistan Becomes First Country to Introduce Typhoid Conjugate Vaccine
events.summary: Pakistan became the first country globally to introduce the WHO-recommended typhoid conjugate vaccine into its routine childhood immunization program, targeting 10 million children.
events.sourceTitle: November 15 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: Albert Hofmann First Synthesizes LSD
events.summary: Swiss chemist Albert Hofmann first synthesized lysergic acid diethylamide (LSD) at Sandoz Laboratories in Basel while researching ergot alkaloid derivatives for circulatory and respiratory stimulation.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine Demonstrates 95.4% Efficacy
events.summary: Moderna announced Phase 3 clinical trial results showing its mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine was 95.4% effective at preventing symptomatic SARS-CoV-2 infection.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Growth Factor Discoverer Stanley Cohen
events.summary: American biochemist Stanley Cohen was born in Brooklyn, New York. He shared the 1986 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine with Rita Levi-Montalcini for discovering epidermal growth factor (EGF) and its role in cell proliferation.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Approves First Therapy to Delay Type 1 Diabetes
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved teplizumab (Tzield), the first disease-modifying immunotherapy shown to delay the clinical onset of type 1 diabetes and insulin dependence by two years or more.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Birth of Vision Neuroscientist George Wald
events.summary: American biochemist and neuroscientist George Wald was born in New York City. He shared the 1967 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating the role of vitamin A and rhodopsin in the primary chemical processes of vision.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Pfizer-BioNTech Reports 95% Efficacy in COVID-19 Vaccine Trial
events.summary: Pfizer and BioNTech announced final Phase 3 clinical trial results from their 44,000-participant study, demonstrating 95% efficacy for their mRNA COVID-19 vaccine.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Cell Biology Pioneer George Emil Palade
events.summary: Romanian-American cell biologist George Emil Palade was born in Iași, Romania. He shared the 1974 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for his discoveries of ribosomes and the structural and functional organization of the cell.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: CDC Reports U.S. HIV-Related Death Rate Halved
events.summary: The CDC published a study showing that the age-adjusted rate of HIV-related deaths among people living with HIV in the United States fell by nearly half between 2010 and 2017 due to early diagnosis and antiretroviral therapy.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Piltdown Man Skull Exposed as a Scientific Hoax
events.summary: The British Natural History Museum announced that the 'Piltdown Man' skull, long thought to be a crucial fossil hominid link, was a deliberate forgery combining a modern human cranium with an orangutan jaw.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: USPSTF Issues Grade 'A' Draft Recommendation for HIV PrEP
events.summary: The U.S. Preventive Services Task Force issued a draft 'A' recommendation advising clinicians to offer pre-exposure prophylaxis (PrEP) to individuals at high risk for HIV infection.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Birth of Gastric Physiology Pioneer William Beaumont
events.summary: American Army surgeon William Beaumont was born in Lebanon, Connecticut. Known as the 'Father of Gastric Physiology,' he conducted landmark direct observations of human digestion through a patient's permanent gastric fistula.
events.sourceTitle: November 21 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: HIV Organ Policy Equity (HOPE) Act Signed into Law
events.summary: President Barack Obama signed the HOPE Act, lifting the federal ban on researching and performing organ transplants from donors with HIV to recipients living with HIV.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: NIH Establishes Neurology and Arthritis Institutes
events.summary: The National Institutes of Health formally established the National Institute of Neurological Diseases and Blindness and the National Institute of Arthritis and Metabolic Diseases under the Omnibus Medical Research Act.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Death of Citric Acid Cycle Discoverer Sir Hans Adolf Krebs
events.summary: German-born British physician and biochemist Sir Hans Adolf Krebs died in Oxford. He won the 1953 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the citric acid cycle (Krebs cycle), the central metabolic pathway of cellular respiration.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Yellow Fever Researcher Walter Reed
events.summary: U.S. Army physician and bacteriologist Walter Reed died in Washington, D.C. He led the U.S. Army Yellow Fever Commission in Cuba that confirmed yellow fever is transmitted by mosquitoes rather than fomites.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Approves First Treatment for Progeria
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved lonafarnib, the first-ever treatment for Hutchinson-Gilford progeria syndrome, a rare fatal genetic disorder causing rapid premature aging in children.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Birth of Spinal Anesthesia Pioneer August Bier
events.summary: German surgeon August Karl Gustav Bier was born in Helsen. He performed the first surgical operation under spinal anesthesia in 1898 and introduced intravenous regional anesthesia (the Bier block) in 1908.
events.sourceTitle: November 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: UNAIDS Reports 17% Global Decline in New HIV Infections
events.summary: UNAIDS released its annual epidemic update reporting a 17% decline in new HIV infections globally over the preceding decade, reflecting expanded prevention and antiretroviral treatment programs.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Birth of Julius Robert von Mayer
events.summary: German physician and physicist Julius Robert von Mayer was born in Heilbronn. Observations of venous blood oxygenation in tropical climates led him to formulate the law of conservation of energy in biological and physical systems.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: CDC Highlights Gaps in U.S. HIV Care Continuum
events.summary: The CDC reported that only 30% of Americans living with HIV had achieved viral suppression in 2011, catalyzing national initiatives to improve retention in care and antiretroviral adherence.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Announcement of First CRISPR Gene-Edited Human Babies
events.summary: Biophysicist He Jiankui announced the birth of twin girls whose embryos had been genetically edited with CRISPR-Cas9 for HIV resistance, prompting widespread international bioethical condemnation and regulatory reforms.
events.sourceTitle: Today in Medical History - November 26th | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: WHO Designates Omicron as a SARS-CoV-2 Variant of Concern
events.summary: The World Health Organization designated the SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant (B.1.1.529), first identified in southern Africa, as a Variant of Concern due to extensive spike-protein mutations and rapid transmissibility.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Alfred Nobel Signs Will Establishing the Nobel Prizes
events.summary: Swedish inventor Alfred Nobel signed his final will in Paris, dedicating his fortune to establish the Nobel Prizes—including the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discoveries conferring the greatest benefit to humankind.
events.sourceTitle: Nobel Prize facts - NobelPrize.org

events.title: Birth of Pediatric Pioneer Fe del Mundo
events.summary: Filipino pediatrician Fe del Mundo was born in Manila. She became the first woman admitted to Harvard Medical School, founded the first pediatric hospital in the Philippines, and designed an improvised bamboo incubator for rural clinics.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/November - Wikipedia

events.title: Cocoanut Grove Fire Transforms Modern Burn Care
events.summary: The Cocoanut Grove nightclub fire in Boston killed 492 people and led surgeons Charles Lund and Newton Browder to develop the age-adjusted Lund-Browder chart for accurately estimating total body surface area burned.
events.sourceTitle: November 28 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Elizabeth Glaser Establishes the Pediatric AIDS Foundation
events.summary: Elizabeth Glaser founded the Pediatric AIDS Foundation to accelerate research into pediatric HIV treatments and establish clinical protocols preventing mother-to-child transmission.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: First Blalock-Taussig Shunt Surgery for Blue Baby Syndrome
events.summary: At Johns Hopkins Hospital, surgeon Alfred Blalock and surgical technician Vivien Thomas, guided by pediatric cardiologist Helen Taussig, performed the first palliative shunt operation to treat Tetralogy of Fallot ('blue baby syndrome').
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History – November 29 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of E. coli Discoverer Theodor Escherich
events.summary: German-Austrian pediatrician and bacteriologist Theodor Escherich was born in Ansbach. He discovered the bacterium Escherichia coli (E. coli) in 1885 and advanced infant nutrition and pediatric infectious disease research.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History – November 29 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Biophysicist Jagadish Chandra Bose
events.summary: Indian polymath, physicist, and biophysicist Sir Jagadish Chandra Bose was born in Bikrampur. He pioneered electrophysiology and demonstrated electrical signaling in living plant tissues.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - November 30 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: amfAR Launches Institute for HIV Cure Research
events.summary: The Foundation for AIDS Research (amfAR) announced the establishment of the amfAR Institute for HIV Cure Research at the University of California, San Francisco, backed by a $100 million cure-research commitment.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: First Global Observance of World AIDS Day
events.summary: Designated by the World Health Organization and supported by the United Nations, the first World AIDS Day was observed worldwide under the theme 'Join the Worldwide Effort' to raise awareness and combat stigma.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Birth of G-Protein Discoverer Martin Rodbell
events.summary: American biochemist and molecular endocrinologist Martin Rodbell was born in Baltimore. He shared the 1994 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering G-proteins and their role in cellular signal transduction.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - December 1 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Birth of Anemia Pioneer George Richards Minot
events.summary: American physician George Richards Minot was born in Boston. He shared the 1934 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering that liver therapy effectively treats pernicious anemia.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Pan American Sanitary Bureau Established
events.summary: The Pan American Sanitary Bureau (precursor to the Pan American Health Organization) was established, marking the start of formal international public health cooperation in the Americas.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: First Successful Human-to-Human Heart Transplant
events.summary: South African cardiac surgeon Christiaan Barnard performed the world's first successful human heart transplant on patient Louis Washkansky at Groote Schuur Hospital in Cape Town.
events.sourceTitle: December 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: First Recorded Successful Separation of Conjoined Twins
events.summary: Swiss surgeon Johannes Fatio completed the first documented successful separation of conjoined twins (Elizabeth and Catherine Meyerin) in Basel using a staged ligature technique over nine days.
events.sourceTitle: December 3 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Oral Contraceptive Pill Made Available on Britain's NHS
events.summary: The female oral contraceptive pill became available through the National Health Service in Great Britain, transforming reproductive medicine and family planning.
events.sourceTitle: December 4 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: First Birth After Deceased-Donor Uterus Transplant
events.summary: Physicians in São Paulo, Brazil, reported the world's first successful live birth resulting from a uterus transplanted from a deceased donor.
events.sourceTitle: December 4 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Glycogen Metabolism Pioneer Carl Ferdinand Cori
events.summary: Czech-American biochemist and pharmacologist Carl Ferdinand Cori was born in Prague. Together with his wife Gerty Cori, he won the 1947 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the catalytic conversion of glycogen (the Cori cycle).
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Great Smog of London Public Health Crisis Begins
events.summary: A severe temperature inversion trapped coal smoke and air pollution over London for five days, causing an estimated 12,000 deaths from respiratory and cardiovascular complications and prompting the UK Clean Air Act.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: First Human Heart Transplant in the United States
events.summary: Cardiac surgeon Adrian Kantrowitz performed the first human heart transplant in the United States at Maimonides Medical Center in Brooklyn, New York, on a newborn infant with Ebstein anomaly.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - December 6 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Anatomical Pathology Founder Giovanni Battista Morgagni
events.summary: Italian anatomist Giovanni Battista Morgagni died in Padua. His landmark work correlating clinical symptoms with post-mortem organ lesions established modern anatomical pathology.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: First Successful Human Corneal Transplant
events.summary: Austrian ophthalmologist Eduard Zirm performed the world's first successful full-thickness human corneal transplant (keratoplasty), restoring partial vision to a man blinded by lime burns.
events.sourceTitle: History of Surgery: A Timeline | Britannica

events.title: Birth of Cell Theory Co-Founder Theodor Schwann
events.summary: German physiologist Theodor Schwann was born in Neuss. He co-founded cell theory, discovered the digestive enzyme pepsin, and identified the myelin-producing Schwann cells of the peripheral nervous system.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Physiologist and Inoculation Advocate Jan Ingenhousz
events.summary: Dutch-British physician and physiologist Jan Ingenhousz was born in Breda. Best known for discovering photosynthesis, he was also a leading European advocate of smallpox inoculation who inoculated the Austrian imperial family.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Authorizes Evusheld for COVID-19 Pre-Exposure Prophylaxis
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization for AstraZeneca's monoclonal antibody combination Evusheld to protect immunocompromised individuals against COVID-19.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Global Eradication of Smallpox Certified
events.summary: An international commission of scientists certified that smallpox had been eradicated worldwide, making it the first human infectious disease eliminated through coordinated global vaccination.
events.sourceTitle: Science on This Day: December 9 | Smallpox Eradication

events.title: First Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine Awarded
events.summary: German physiologist Emil von Behring received the inaugural Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for his work on serum therapy, particularly its application against diphtheria.
events.sourceTitle: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 1901 - NobelPrize.org

events.title: Watson, Crick, and Wilkins Receive Nobel Prize for DNA Structure
events.summary: Francis Crick, James Watson, and Maurice Wilkins were awarded the Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine in Stockholm for discovering the molecular double-helix structure of DNA.
events.sourceTitle: The Nobel Prize Award Ceremony 1962 - NobelPrize.org

events.title: Birth of Bacteriology Founder Robert Koch
events.summary: German physician and microbiologist Robert Koch was born in Clausthal. He identified the causative bacteria of anthrax, tuberculosis, and cholera, formulated Koch's postulates, and won the 1905 Nobel Prize.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Issues First EUA for a COVID-19 Vaccine (Pfizer-BioNTech)
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued its first Emergency Use Authorization for a COVID-19 vaccine, authorizing the Pfizer-BioNTech mRNA vaccine for individuals ages 16 and older.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Emil von Behring Delivers First Medicine Nobel Lecture
events.summary: Emil von Behring delivered his Nobel Lecture 'Serum Therapy in Therapeutics and Medical Science' in Stockholm, outlining the immunological principles behind passive immunization.
events.sourceTitle: Emil von Behring - Wikipedia

events.title: First Cluster of COVID-19 Symptoms Appears in Wuhan
events.summary: A cluster of patients in Wuhan, China, began experiencing symptoms of an atypical pneumonia-like illness unresponsive to standard treatments, later identified as COVID-19 caused by SARS-CoV-2.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Claude Beck Publishes First Human Open-Chest Defibrillation
events.summary: Cardiac surgeon Claude Schaeffer Beck published in JAMA the first report of successful open-chest electrical defibrillation in a human, reversing prolonged ventricular fibrillation in a 14-year-old boy.
events.sourceTitle: December 13 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Pasteur Institute Files Suit Over HIV Discovery Recognition
events.summary: The Pasteur Institute filed suit in the U.S. Court of Claims seeking formal recognition that French researchers were the first to discover the AIDS virus and requesting shared patent rights to HIV blood tests.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: First Public COVID-19 Vaccine Administered in the United States
events.summary: New York intensive care nurse Sandra Lindsay became the first person in the United States outside of clinical trials to receive an authorized COVID-19 vaccine.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Geneticist Edward Tatum
events.summary: American geneticist Edward Lawrie Tatum was born in Boulder, Colorado. He shared the 1958 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for showing that genes act by regulating specific chemical events ('one gene, one enzyme').
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: APA Removes Homosexuality from List of Mental Disorders
events.summary: The American Psychiatric Association voted to remove homosexuality from its Diagnostic and Statistical Manual of Mental Disorders (DSM), marking a landmark shift in psychiatric medicine.
events.sourceTitle: December 15 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Birth of Phototherapy Pioneer Niels Ryberg Finsen
events.summary: Faroese-Danish physician Niels Ryberg Finsen was born in Tórshavn. He received the 1903 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for developing concentrated light radiation therapy (phototherapy) to treat lupus vulgaris.
events.sourceTitle: December 15 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: UK National Insurance Act Becomes Law
events.summary: The United Kingdom's National Insurance Act of 1911 became law, establishing compulsory health insurance for millions of British industrial workers and laying the foundation for national healthcare.
events.sourceTitle: December 16 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: U.S. Halts 1976 Swine Flu Vaccination Program
events.summary: The U.S. government suspended its nationwide swine flu immunization campaign following reports of Guillain-Barré syndrome paralysis among vaccine recipients.
events.sourceTitle: December 16 in Medical History - SolvedPGSS

events.title: CDC Reports Unexplained Immunodeficiency in Infants
events.summary: The CDC published an MMWR report documenting 22 cases of unexplained cellular immunodeficiency and opportunistic infections in infants, an early milestone in recognizing pediatric AIDS.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: CDC Records Highest 12-Month U.S. Drug Overdose Toll
events.summary: The CDC reported over 81,000 drug overdose deaths in the United States during the 12-month period ending May 2020—the highest annual total recorded to that date—driven largely by synthetic opioids.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: FDA Grants EUA for Moderna COVID-19 Vaccine
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration issued an Emergency Use Authorization for Moderna's mRNA-1273 COVID-19 vaccine, co-developed with scientists at the NIH National Institute of Allergy and Infectious Diseases.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Oncogene Pioneer Harold E. Varmus
events.summary: American physician-scientist Harold E. Varmus was born in Oceanside, New York. He shared the 1989 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the cellular origin of retroviral oncogenes and later served as NIH Director.
events.sourceTitle: December 18 in Medical History | SolvedPGSS

events.title: Death of Neuropathologist Alois Alzheimer
events.summary: German psychiatrist and neuropathologist Alois Alzheimer died in Breslau. In 1906, he first described the clinical and neuropathological features of 'presenile dementia,' now known as Alzheimer's disease.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Immunogeneticist George Davis Snell
events.summary: American geneticist George Davis Snell was born in Bradford, Massachusetts. He shared the 1980 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering the major histocompatibility complex (MHC), fundamental to organ transplantation.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Doctors Without Borders (MSF) Founded in Paris
events.summary: Médecins Sans Frontières (Doctors Without Borders) was founded in Paris by French physicians and journalists to provide independent emergency medical aid in conflict and disaster zones.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - December 20, 2016 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: Death of Neurophysiologist Sir Alan Lloyd Hodgkin
events.summary: British physiologist and biophysicist Sir Alan Lloyd Hodgkin died in Cambridge. He shared the 1963 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for elucidating the ionic mechanisms underlying nerve action potentials.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of James Parkinson
events.summary: English surgeon and apothecary James Parkinson died in London. His 1817 'Essay on the Shaking Palsy' provided the first systematic clinical description of the neurodegenerative disorder now known as Parkinson's disease.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Approves First Long-Acting Injectable HIV PrEP
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration approved cabotegravir extended-release injectable suspension (Apretude), the first long-acting injectable medication for HIV pre-exposure prophylaxis administered every two months.
events.sourceTitle: A Timeline of HIV and AIDS | HIV.gov

events.title: Birth of BCG Vaccine Co-Developer Camille Guérin
events.summary: French veterinarian and bacteriologist Camille Guérin was born in Poitiers. Working with Albert Calmette, he developed the Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) vaccine against tuberculosis.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: FDA Authorizes First Oral Antiviral Pill for COVID-19 (Paxlovid)
events.summary: The U.S. Food and Drug Administration granted Emergency Use Authorization for Pfizer's Paxlovid (nirmatrelvir/ritonavir), the first at-home oral antiviral treatment for high-risk COVID-19 patients.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: First Successful Human Kidney Transplant Performed
events.summary: Surgeon Dr. Joseph E. Murray performed the world's first successful human kidney transplant between identical twins at Peter Bent Brigham Hospital in Boston, launching modern organ transplantation and earning the 1990 Nobel Prize.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: National Cancer Act of 1971 Signed into Law
events.summary: President Richard Nixon signed the National Cancer Act of 1971, launching the modern U.S. National Cancer Program and establishing comprehensive cancer centers and expanded federal oncology research.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Death of Neurologist Vladimir Bekhterev
events.summary: Russian neurologist Vladimir Mikhailovich Bekhterev died in Moscow. He is renowned for describing ankylosing spondylitis (Bekhterew disease), studying spinal reflexes, and identifying the hippocampus's role in memory.
events.sourceTitle: December 24 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Immunologist and Public Health Leader Anthony Fauci
events.summary: American physician-scientist Anthony S. Fauci was born in Brooklyn, New York. As long-serving director of NIAID, he pioneered vasculitis therapy and led U.S. biomedical responses to HIV/AIDS, Ebola, and COVID-19.
events.sourceTitle: Anthony Fauci - Wikipedia

events.title: Birth of Cancer Pathologist James Stephen Ewing
events.summary: American pathologist James Stephen Ewing was born in Pittsburgh. A pioneer in oncology and founder of the American Association for Cancer Research, he first described the malignant bone tumor known as Ewing sarcoma in 1921.
events.sourceTitle: December 25 – On This Day in Medical History - LITFL

events.title: Birth of Electron Microscope Inventor Ernst Ruska
events.summary: German physicist Ernst Ruska was born in Heidelberg. His invention of the electron microscope (1986 Nobel Prize) enabled direct visualization of viruses, organelles, and ultrastructural pathology.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Marie and Pierre Curie Announce Discovery of Radium
events.summary: Marie and Pierre Curie announced the isolation of radium to the French Academy of Sciences, laying the scientific foundation for brachytherapy and modern radiation oncology.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: National Eye Institute Established at NIH
events.summary: The National Eye Institute was formally established at the National Institutes of Health to lead federal biomedical research into vision disorders and blindness.
events.sourceTitle: Chronology of Events | National Institutes of Health (NIH)

events.title: Birth of Microbiology Pioneer Louis Pasteur
events.summary: French chemist and microbiologist Louis Pasteur was born in Dole. His breakthroughs in germ theory, pasteurization, and vaccines for anthrax and rabies revolutionized infectious disease medicine.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: First Use of Ether Anesthesia for Childbirth
events.summary: American physician Dr. Crawford Williamson Long administered diethyl ether anesthesia during childbirth for the first time in Jefferson, Georgia, delivering his own child painlessly.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Röntgen Publishes Paper Announcing X-Rays
events.summary: Wilhelm Conrad Röntgen submitted his landmark paper 'On a New Kind of Rays' detailing the discovery of X-rays, inaugurating modern diagnostic medical imaging.
events.sourceTitle: Today In Medical History - December 28 | Medical News Bulletin

events.title: First American IVF Baby Born in Virginia
events.summary: Elizabeth Jordan Carr, the first baby conceived through in vitro fertilization (IVF) in the United States, was born in Norfolk, Virginia, advancing reproductive endocrinology.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of 'English Hippocrates' Thomas Sydenham
events.summary: English physician Thomas Sydenham died in London. Celebrated for empirical bedside observation, he wrote classic clinical descriptions of gout, scarlet fever, and Sydenham chorea.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Neurotransmitter Pioneer Julius Axelrod
events.summary: American biochemist Julius Axelrod died in Rockville, Maryland. He shared the 1970 Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine for discovering how catecholamine neurotransmitters are stored, released, and inactivated.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: Death of Pneumatic Chemistry Pioneer Jan Baptist van Helmont
events.summary: Flemish physician and chemist Jan Baptist van Helmont died in Vilvoorde. He coined the term 'gas,' pioneered quantitative physiological experiments, and challenged humoral medicine.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: UK Authorizes Oxford-AstraZeneca COVID-19 Vaccine
events.summary: The United Kingdom granted emergency use authorization to the Oxford University–AstraZeneca COVID-19 vaccine, enabling rapid rollout of a refrigerator-stable viral vector vaccine.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline

events.title: Birth of Modern Anatomy Founder Andreas Vesalius
events.summary: Flemish anatomist and physician Andreas Vesalius was born in Brussels. His 1543 masterwork 'De humani corporis fabrica' overturned centuries of Galenic dogma and established modern human anatomy based on direct dissection.
events.sourceTitle: Portal:History of science/Selected anniversaries/December - Wikipedia

events.title: WHO Informed of Pneumonia Cluster in Wuhan
events.summary: The World Health Organization Country Office in China was officially informed of cases of pneumonia of unknown etiology in Wuhan, marking the start of international tracking of the COVID-19 pandemic.
events.sourceTitle: CDC Museum COVID-19 Timeline
